question.text: Which of the following is TRUE about the Corporate Debt Market Development Fund (CDMDF)?

answer.text: It is an open-ended AIF with 5-year tenure
It is a close-ended AIF with 15-year tenure formed as a trust
It invests only in equity securities
It is classified under Category III AIF

explanation.text: The Logic: CDMDF is a close-ended AIF formed as a trust with a 15-year tenure from the date of its first closing. It is classified under Category I AIF and its units are issued to AMCs and specified debt-oriented mutual fund schemes. The Trap: Despite being a debt-related fund, CDMDF sits under Category I (not Category II) because it serves a broader economic purpose — acting as a backstop facility. The 15-year tenure is much longer than typical AIF tenures. Note: CDMDF's Category I classification reflects its role as a backstop facility for the corporate bond market rather than a return-seeking debt vehicle.
